To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) basal dendrites are present in the adult intrahippocamapal kainic model of epilepsy, 2) basal dendrites form recurrent excitatory circuits, 3) the presence of basal dendrites is not related to increased neurogenesis and 4) basal dendrites may contribute to hyper‐excitability in this model of epilepsy.

Abnormalities of granular dendritic morphology, including formation of basal dendritic processes, are present in the dentate gyrus of rats with kainic acid‐induced status epilepticus despite a reduced rate of postinjury neurogenic cell proliferation.

the intrahippocompal kainic acid rat model of epilepsy has abnormal granule cell basal dendritic morphology despite the fact that the model is associated with reduced postinjury hippocampal neurogenesis.
